findings.title: Live translation API key is hardcoded in client-side code and shipped to every browser.
Review body and translated text are injected as raw HTML, allowing stored XSS.
Authors are fetched one by one in a sequential loop (N+1 requests, awaited serially).
Fetch of reviews has no res.ok check, no try/catch and no error state, so a failure leaves the spinner forever or throws an unhandled rejection; JSON is cast without validation.
Effect has an empty dependency array so reviews are not reloaded when productId changes, and there is no abort/ignore flag so stale responses can overwrite newer ones.
Translate control is a clickable div, not a button, so it is not keyboard accessible or announced as an action.
productId is interpolated into the URL path without encodeURIComponent.
Debug console.log left in, dumping review and author data to the console.
Translation failure message is stored as the review text and then rendered through innerHTML in place of the review body, replacing the original; also translated cache ignores targetLanguage changes.
deleteTask server action performs no session or membership check, so any caller can delete any task by id.
findings.evidence: const { projectId } = await db.task.delete({ where: { id }, select: { projectId: true } });

findings.title: QueryClient is created at module scope and shared across all server requests, so prefetched data of one user is dehydrated into another user's response.
findings.evidence: const serverQueryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 60_000 } } });

findings.title: Optimistic update has no snapshot and no onError rollback, so a failed move leaves the UI showing the wrong status until refetch.
Search effect has no cancellation or ignore flag, so out-of-order responses can show results for an older term (race condition).
`columnTasks.length && (...)` renders a literal 0 in empty columns.
Effect uses updatedAt but has an empty dependency array, so the label stays stale when the task is updated.
Array index used as React key for task cards, so card state (e.g. delete confirmation) can attach to the wrong task when order changes.
Server actions marked 'use server' live in the same module as client hooks and components, which Next.js does not allow for a 'use server' file and mixes server and client concerns.
